summary_responses.response: The United States Department of Justice Office of Justice Programs has proposed a new Privacy Act system of records titled JUSTICE/OJP-017 for the Bureau of Justice Statistics Statistical Data. It covers a broad range of individuals including household survey respondents, inmates, probationers and parolees, arrestees, juveniles in placement and decedents in custody, and holds sensitive data such as names, addresses, Social Security numbers, criminal histories, victimization details, medical and employment information and immigration court records. The notice is effective upon publication but invites public comments on routine uses through November 16 2026 directed to the Office of Privacy and Civil Liberties.

summary_responses.response: The Department of the Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service issued a final rule amending 31 CFR Part 356, the Uniform Offering Circular governing auctions of marketable Treasury bills, notes, and bonds, effective October 15, 2026, though changes to noncompetitive customer bid requirements will apply only when Treasury's upgraded auction system goes live. The amendments clarify definitions for adjusted value, dated date, index ratio, issue date, and settlement amount without altering calculations for inflation-protected securities and remove outdated references to the former CUSIP issuer, paper bids, and inflation-indexed securities terminology. They also align the rule's language with current auction announcements and results by standardizing references to high yield, high discount rate, or high discount margin and replacing terms such as accept and tender with award and recognize. The most substantive operational change requires submitters to provide each individual customer's name and bid amount prior to the noncompetitive auction close, eliminating the prior practice of submitting summary bid amounts in order to allow earlier finalization of post-auction operations. Finally, the rule replaces a specific TreasuryDirect URL reference with general website posting for auction results and is exempt from notice-and-comment and Regulatory Flexibility Act requirements as a contract-related and non-significant action.

summary_responses.response: Researchers from Tel Aviv University and Columbia University propose DiffTry, a lightweight distributed mechanism that transforms standard microservice retries into a rejection prioritization system to protect high-value transactions during overloads. They note that independently scaled microservices often become miscoordinated, causing temporary overloads where valuable requests are rejected and where attackers can intentionally flood low-priority traffic to inflict economic damage, while conventional uniform retries fail to protect important traffic and can trigger performance-degrading retry storms. DiffTry addresses this by assigning different retry attempt limits to different priority classes at the sender side, for example allowing premium requests more retries than low-priority ones, requiring no overload sensing, coordination, or application changes and remaining effectively silent when the system is not overloaded. The authors develop analytical models for both a single overloaded service and for general networks of services, deriving per-class throughput and rejection rates, proving convergence and monotonicity properties and showing uniqueness of solutions for directed acyclic graphs that cover many real deployments. Simulations and a live Kubernetes service-mesh deployment validate the analysis, showing that under overload high-priority traffic can achieve around 15 percent rejection and account for about 85 percent of successful completions despite representing only half the load, closely matching theoretical predictions.

summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management has issued a direct final rule amending its title 5 Family and Medical Leave Act regulations to incorporate statutory changes enacted in January 2021 and December 2023. The rule will take effect December 14 2026 unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16 2026, in which case the Office of Personnel Management will withdraw the affected provisions and pursue normal notice and comment rulemaking. The amendments expand FMLA eligibility by counting virtually all federal civilian service, including temporary, intermittent, Postal Service, Postal Regulatory Commission and nonappropriated fund instrumentality service, and honorable active duty service in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Space Force or Marine Corps toward the 12 month service requirement. The rule also clarifies that employees may substitute annual or sick leave earned under non-title 5 authorities for unpaid FMLA leave. In addition it excludes Veterans Health Administration employees covered by a leave system under title 38 from title 5 FMLA coverage and notes that because paid parental leave requires FMLA eligibility, the expanded service credit also broadens access to paid parental leave.
